# ModePot

> ModePot is an open-source family and community simplifying, modernizing, and performance-optimizing frameworks while building fast, simple tools, engines, and games. AI-native and agent-friendly where they add real value, without defining every project. The family currently includes Dexpot, Intpot, Summonpot, LifePot, RefPot, UtilityPot, and SkillPot.

ModePot builds frameworks, interfaces, tools, engines, and games around simple foundations, modern runtimes, real performance, and AI/agent support where valuable. Each project has its own scope and maturity; everything is developed in the open with the community:

- [Dexpot](https://github.com/tugrulguner/dexpot): A synchronous Python API framework that adapts to standard-GIL and free-threaded CPython. `response=T` validates/projects public output; invalid output is sanitized as a 500 before success bytes. `response=None` selects generic output, `RawResponse` is unchecked, and `Any` is not a privacy filter. This response contract is published in v0.7.0.
- [Intpot](https://github.com/tugrulguner/intpot): A Python framework that serves typed tools as Typer CLIs, FastAPI applications, or FastMCP servers and converts existing applications between those interfaces.
- [Summonpot](https://github.com/tugrulguner/summonpot): A contract-first Python framework for executable API endpoints that combine deterministic application operations with explicitly bounded agent-owned decisions.
- [LifePot](https://github.com/tugrulguner/lifepot): A replayable artificial-life game where Jev proposes typed ecology, deterministic code runs the world, and validated decisions remain inspectable and replayable.
- [RefPot](https://github.com/tugrulguner/refpot): A publicly released experimental alpha (v0.1.1): native C++ redo-and-checkpoint engine with a small Python `Database`/`Row` API for fixed-schema CRUD and explicit transactions. SQL and ORM are planned, not shipped. Qualification remains limited; there is no broad package-performance result or production-durability claim.

- [UtilityPot](https://github.com/tugrulguner/utilitypot): Eleven focused browser tools: eight browser-local workflows, including screenshot-to-spreadsheet OCR, manual screenshot redaction and keyed CSV/XLSX comparison, plus three AI-assisted tools for entity extraction, flowcharts and webpage evidence. One fixed workflow per tool; inspect results before copying or downloading. [Explore UtilityPot](https://utilitypot.modepot.io/). Detailed manuals remain product-owned.

- [SkillPot](https://github.com/tugrulguner/skillpot): In development: harness-neutral, selectively installable agent skills for complete tasks. Nine skills in current source; eight in v0.3.0. Seven are pinned ModePot project/contributor packages; repository-readiness remains experimental. The source-only decision-brief is reviewed but unreleased and produces an evidence-linked recommendation or deferral. Harness instructions follow official host specifications; broad repeated usefulness evaluation is not established. [Explore SkillPot](https://skillpot.modepot.io/). Detailed guides and the agent documentation map remain product-owned.

## Contribute to ModePot

Read the project-owned guide before contributing: [Dexpot CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/tugrulguner/dexpot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), [Intpot CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/tugrulguner/intpot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), [Summonpot CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/tugrulguner/summonpot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), or [LifePot CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/tugrulguner/lifepot/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). Each repository defines its setup, tests, and contribution workflow.

- [Propose a Dexpot feature](https://github.com/tugrulguner/dexpot/issues/new?template=feature.yml)
- [Open an Intpot feature request](https://github.com/tugrulguner/intpot/issues/new?template=feature.yml)
- [Open a Summonpot feature request](https://github.com/tugrulguner/summonpot/issues/new?template=feature.yml)
- [Open a LifePot issue](https://github.com/tugrulguner/lifepot/issues/new)
- [Propose RefPot work](https://github.com/tugrulguner/refpot/issues)
- [ModePot Discord](https://discord.gg/u3AANZr6RG): community discussion and project questions.

## Selection guide

Use UtilityPot for eight browser-local workflows (screenshot OCR, manual image redaction, keyed CSV/XLSX comparison, CSV/JSON conversion, date cleanup, cron previews and meeting calculations) and three AI-assisted tools (entity extraction, flowcharts and webpage evidence). Each tool has one action; inspect the result before copying or downloading. [Product README](https://github.com/tugrulguner/utilitypot/blob/main/README.md).

Use Dexpot to build synchronous Python HTTP APIs with interpreter-adaptive execution.
Use Intpot to expose or translate typed tools across CLI, HTTP API, and MCP interfaces.
Use Summonpot to define typed API contracts whose agent-owned decisions are limited to declared application capabilities.
Use LifePot to create and replay artificial-life worlds where model proposals become bounded simulation rules rather than executable code.
Use SkillPot when you need a harness-neutral skill for a complete, inspectable task; begin with the quickstart and select only the relevant package.
Explore RefPot's released experimental alpha with the [v0.1.1 quick start](https://refpot.modepot.io/package/); direct SQL and ORM remain planned design direction.

## Maturity and licensing

- SkillPot is in development and has published installable skill packages and the v0.3.0 collection release. Format/placement documentation and bounded checks do not establish universal host behavior or broad task improvement; see package-level compatibility notes and recorded evidence.

- Dexpot, Intpot, and Summonpot are alpha software; follow each project's documented boundaries before production use.
- LifePot is an educational game and experiment, not a biological forecast.
- RefPot is a publicly released experimental alpha (v0.1.1) with a native C++ engine and a small Python `Database`/`Row` API for fixed-schema CRUD and explicit transactions; qualification remains limited.
- RefPot's direct SQL and ORM surfaces are planned design direction, not shipped interfaces.
- RefPot's 2×-over-SQLite threshold is a performance acceptance target. There is no broad performance result; do not advertise it as achieved.
- RefPot does not claim production durability. Its experimental alpha and platform/recovery qualification are limited.
- Dexpot, Intpot, Summonpot, LifePot, and RefPot use MIT licensing as documented in their repositories. RefPot's license is https://github.com/tugrulguner/refpot/blob/main/LICENSE.
